claims.text: At temperatures of at least 1000 K, equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than commercially pure tungsten.
At temperatures of at least 1000 K, equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater toughness than commercially pure tungsten.
The multicomponent refractory configuration of WTaTiVZr produces significant lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr enhances dislocation nucleation and multiplication at high temperature.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr enhances dynamic recovery at high temperature.
Enhanced dislocation activity and dynamic recovery delay crack nucleation and propagation in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
The alloy has the equimolar composition W20Ta20Ti20V20Zr20.
As-synthesized equimolar WTaTiVZr has a BCC structure.
The WTaTiVZr and pure-tungsten specimens are homogeneous before testing.
Lattice distortions and nanoscale compositional fluctuations impede dislocation motion in WTaTiVZr.
The lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr activates multiple slip systems and facilitates dislocation cross-slip at high temperature.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will have a higher density of mobile dislocations than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will show more dislocation rearrangement and cross-slip than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, plastic deformation will be more homogeneous in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten will show limited dislocation mobility and earlier crack initiation than WTaTiVZr under the specified conditions.

The proposed toughening mechanism is expected to apply only at high temperatures and plasma-facing-relevant strain rates, and may not apply at lower temperatures or substantially different strain rates.
Refractory high-entropy alloys have previously shown substantial mechanical strength or ductility at elevated temperatures.
The lattice-distortion mechanism proposed for WTaTiVZr is well supported by high-entropy-alloy literature.
